binders: m is an arbitrary natural number, possibly zero.
q is an arbitrary function ℝ → ℝ → (Fin m → ℝ), equivalently an m-component real-valued function of two real variables.
coefficient is an arbitrary real matrix with rows and columns indexed by Fin m.
x and t are arbitrary real numbers.
conclusions: LocalDef001 q coefficient x t holds if and only if there exist vectors qt,qx ∈ ℝ^m such that the one-variable map τ ↦ q(x,τ) has derivative qt at t, the one-variable map ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) has derivative qx at x, and qt + coefficient·qx = 0.
Equivalently, the final equation says that for every i ∈ Fin m, qt_i + ∑_{j ∈ Fin m} coefficient_{ij} qx_j = 0.
mathematical_definitions: Fin m is the index set {0,…,m-1}, so Fin m → ℝ is the space of m-component real vectors.
A Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ is an m-by-m real matrix represented by its entries coefficient_{ij}.
HasDerivAt (fun τ => q x τ) qt t means that the partial map obtained by fixing x is differentiable at t with vector derivative qt.
HasDerivAt (fun ξ => q ξ t) qx x means that the partial map obtained by fixing t is differentiable at x with vector derivative qx.
coefficient.mulVec qx is ordinary finite matrix-vector multiplication, and vector addition and zero are componentwise.
LocalDef001 is an abbreviation for LocalDef002, and LocalDef002 is precisely the existential conjunction appearing on the right side of the equivalence.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every dimension m, every m-component function q defined on ℝ², every real m-by-m matrix coefficient, and every point (x,t), the predicate LocalDef001 q coefficient x t is equivalent to the existence of the two separate partial-derivative vectors qt = ∂q/∂t at (x,t) and qx = ∂q/∂x at (x,t), satisfying the vector equation qt + coefficient·qx = 0. Since LocalDef001 abbreviates LocalDef002 and LocalDef002 is exactly this condition, the proposition is a definitional characterization rather than an additional analytical result.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: No positivity assumption on m is present. When m = 0, Fin m is empty, the vector and matrix types are zero-dimensional, and the componentwise equation has no components; the derivative conditions likewise degenerate to maps into the singleton empty-function space.
No continuity or differentiability is assumed globally or on a neighborhood; only the two separate one-variable derivatives at the single selected point are required.
Separate partial differentiability is encoded, not joint Fréchet differentiability of q as a function ℝ² → ℝ^m.
The coefficient matrix is completely arbitrary: no invertibility, symmetry, positivity, hyperbolicity, or other structural property is required.
The coefficient is a fixed matrix parameter and the proposition does not encode coefficients depending on x, t, or q.

There are no initial conditions, boundary conditions, spatial or temporal domain restrictions, uniqueness claims, existence claims for solutions, or regularity beyond the displayed pointwise derivative witnesses.

The target universally quantifies q and the point (x,t), but the equivalence itself does not assert that the derivative witnesses exist; when they do not, both sides are false because LocalDef001 is defined by the same existential condition.

Because the left side merely abbreviates the right side, the theorem does not derive the differential equation from independent assumptions or prove any substantive equivalence between distinct notions.
